The research outlines a strategy to transform the `local-delegate` MCP from a personal, hardcoded setup into a professional, publishable Python package. The core objective is to decouple the tool from specific local paths and hardware, turning it into a generic client for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

The recommended distribution method is via PyPI, executable through `uvx`, and registered in the official MCP registry. To achieve this, the project must undergo a "greenfield" refactor in a new directory, `D:\Projects\local-delegate`, to avoid breaking the current working installation. Key technical changes include replacing hardcoded `D:\` paths with environment variables, making the `llama-swap` autostart optional, and moving personal integrations (like the 27 sub-agents) to a documentation "recipes" section. # Shared Daemon

## Why it exists

The `stdio` MCP transport requires a process per client, which causes the embedded dashboard to die when the process holding port `9393` terminates. `local-delegate serve` solves this by maintaining a single persistent process per user that serves both MCP Streamable HTTP and the dashboard.

## Startup

```powershell
uvx local-delegate-mcp serve
```

Defaults include MCP at `http://127.0.0.1:9393/mcp`, the dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:9393/`, and status at `http://127.0.0.1:9393/api/daemon`. Users can configure `--host`, `--port`, and `--log-level`. Backend environment variables must belong to the daemon process.

## Clients

Clients like Codex, Claude Code, and opencode should all be configured against the same URL. The daemon manages global backpressure via `LOCAL_DELEGATE_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`.

## llama-swap seen from the daemon

The daemon manages model "turns" if a local `llama-swap` is used, preventing VRAM conflicts. It provides several endpoints for the CLI and `doctor`, such as `GET /api/llamaswap/status` and `POST /api/llamaswap/watch`.

## Port Authentication

By default, the port is open on loopback. To secure it, define `LOCAL_DELEGATE_WEB_TOKEN`. The daemon supports `Authorization: Bearer`, `Authorization: Basic`, and `Cookie: ld_session=…` for browser sessions.
